answers.answer: A player rules a clearing by having more total warriors plus buildings there than each other player; tokens and pawns do not count. An ordinary tie means no one rules. Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle: rule 2.5.

answers.answer: A normal move takes any positive number of the player's warriors or pawns along a path to an adjacent clearing, and the player must rule the origin or destination or both. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including on multiple moves in one action; rule is rechecked for each move. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.
answers.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle: Move (4.2).

answers.answer: Battle order: defender may play one matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush. The defender's ambush is discarded; if foiled it deals no hits, otherwise it deals two immediate hits, not capped by defending warriors. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends immediately. Resolve before-roll effects, roll (higher die is attacker's hits, lower is defender's; Alliance defending reverses dice), then resolve after-roll effects. Rolled hits are capped by each side's own warriors in battle, except Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors. Add extra hits without a warrior cap and subtract ignored hits. If defender has no warriors, attacker gets one defenseless hit; Vagabond is defenseless only with no undamaged swords. For each side's removals, its owner chooses the order, but all warriors must be removed before buildings/tokens; hits are dealt by both sides and losing warriors does not change the roll cap retroactively. Whoever removes an enemy building or token scores one VP each, including a defender and outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage.
answers.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle: Battle (4.3), six steps.

answers.answer: Crafting uses the card's bottom-left crafting icons, not its suit; each crafting piece can activate once per turn, except Vagabond may reactivate its pawn by exhausting more hammers. If an item card's item is absent from the map supply, it cannot be crafted. A persistent effect cannot be crafted if an identical persistent effect is already in the player's play area.
answers.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle: Craft (4.1).

answers.answer: During the player's own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, they may activate a dominance card from hand, remove their score marker, and stop scoring VP. At the start of their own Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if they rule three clearings of that suit; bird dominance wins if they rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. An activated dominance card cannot be removed or replaced.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — Dominance (3.3).

answers.answer: When a dominance card would enter the discard pile, put it near the map as available instead. During their own Daylight, a player may spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into hand. An available bird dominance remains a bird card, so it must be paid for with a bird; a bird hand card can pay for a non-bird dominance.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — Dominance (3.3).

answers.answer: For two players, remove all four dominance cards before shuffling the shared deck; each player draws three cards. Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The separate map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, and 2 coins. Keep the four R-marked ruin items separate; only if Vagabond is in the game does its setup hide one each of the R-marked bag, boot, hammer, and sword under the ruins; without Vagabond, ruins contain no items. Set up factions in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond; this order is distinct from turn order.
answers.evidence: Setup — Standard Setup (Law 5.1), steps 3–7; Vagabond setup (9.3).

answers.answer: Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep's clearing, but other players may move pieces into it. When any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply; this also applies outside battle. If there is no Keep, Field Hospitals have no destination. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6) — Keep and Field Hospitals.

answers.answer: Marquise Daylight starts by crafting with workshops, then taking up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order and number except Recruit's limit. March is one compound action of up to two moves. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and may be done only once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6) — Daylight.

answers.answer: To build, choose a clearing Marquise rules with an open building slot and a building type, then take the leftmost building of that type on its track. Pay the column's full wood cost using wood in the target clearing or in other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP shown on the newly uncovered track space. Building requires sufficient wood, an available building, and a legal slot.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6) — Daylight, Build.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, first draw one card if the Eyrie's hand is empty (Emergency Orders). Then add one or two hand cards to the Decree, with at most one bird card, placing each in any column. Finally, if there are no roosts on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7) — Birdsong, in order.

answers.answer: Eyrie crafts with roosts, then resolves every Decree card by columns in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order; within each column it chooses card order freely, and birds are wild. Recruit places a warrior at a roost in a clearing matching the card (two with Charismatic). Move must move at least one warrior from a matching clearing, obeying ordinary movement rules. Battle must start in a matching clearing containing Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build places a roost in a matching clearing Eyrie rules, with an open slot and no roost already there.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7) — Daylight and Decree requirements.

answers.answer: When any required Decree action cannot be completed fully, Eyrie immediately enters Turmoil and does not skip that card or continue other columns. It loses one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discards all Decree cards except Viziers; flips its current leader face down and chooses a face-up replacement (if none are face up, flip all leaders face up first); then retucks Viziers into the new leader's columns. Daylight ends and Evening follows. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings; Evening scoring, drawing, and hand discard still occur.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7) — Turmoil and Evening.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one matching hand card to Supporters per affected move/group (birds count), not per warrior. If they have no matching card, including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, which draws one deck card into Supporters. The supporter capacity still applies; without bases it is five and incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded. Merely battling in sympathy does not trigger it unless sympathy is removed; placing warriors and moving only the Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8) — Outrage and Supporters.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, Alliance performs any number of Revolts first, then any number of Spread Sympathy actions. Revolt chooses a sympathetic clearing with no base whose suit matches a base still on the board; it spends two matching supporters, removes all enemy pieces there, places the matching base, places warriors equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base's printed suit (including the revolt clearing), places one warrior in Officers, and scores normal VP for removed enemy buildings/tokens. Spread Sympathy chooses an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to existing sympathy, or any clearing if no sympathy is on the map. It spends the supporter cost shown above the next sympathy token, plus one matching supporter if the chosen clearing has at least three warriors belonging to one other player (Martial Law); it places the token and scores the uncovered VP. Only one sympathy per clearing, and the Keep's placement ban applies.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8) — Birdsong: Revolt and Spread Sympathy.

answers.answer: To Train, Alliance spends a hand card matching a clearing with a base and places one supply warrior in the Officers box; supporters cannot pay. In Evening, each officer allows one military operation, including Organize: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there, and score the uncovered VP. Organize spends no supporters and has no adjacency or Martial Law requirement, though token placement must be legal. Officers remain on board when used. When a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing, including birds, and remove half the officers rounded up; if no bases remain, reduce supporters to five. Apply this whenever a base is removed.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8) — Losing a base, Daylight Train, Evening operations.

answers.answer: At Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed now adds no refresh this step. Optional Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, and ignores effects preventing movement out of a clearing. Normal Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if the destination has any warriors of a Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest may move only to an adjacent clearing. If in a forest in Evening, Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, moving ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if possible; it does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Vagabond always draws in Evening, including after Rest: one card plus one per face-up coin on track.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3) — Birdsong, Daylight Move, and Evening.

answers.answer: Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing and takes one hidden item face up into Satchel or a matching track; score 1 VP if an item is taken, and remove the ruin once its last item is taken, freeing the slot. Quest chooses a face-up quest matching the clearing and exhausts its two listed items, then places it completed and chooses either VP equal to the number of matching completed quests (including this one) or draws two cards; draw a replacement quest. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel, keeping its current face; ready tea, coins, or bags move to tracks if space allows.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3) — Daylight Explore, Quest, Repair.

answers.answer: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes that faction Hostile, except for the special allied-warrior battle-loss rule. During Vagabond's own-turn battle, Infamy scores one extra VP for each hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; ordinary VP for buildings/tokens still applies. There is no Infamy when defending on another player's turn or for Strike. Aid cannot move a faction out of Hostile, though it can still take a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it instead remove another piece of that faction. Strike is not a battle and gives no Infamy.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3) — Relationships, Hostile, Infamy, Aid, Strike.

answers.answer: With four or more players, during its own Daylight at 10 or more VP, Vagabond may activate dominance to form a coalition with another player not already in a coalition. The partner must have the lowest VP among players other than Vagabond; Vagabond chooses among ties. Vagabond places its score marker on that player's faction board and stops scoring. If the partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including a dominance win. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent; coalition does not itself grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — Vagabond coalition (9.2.8).
